title: Implementation-Defined (Arranged According to the Laws of Sort)
summary: Two live shuffles of twelve squares are tallied side by side: honest chance fades to grey, while the web's favourite sort-shuffle develops a portrait of your JavaScript engine.
mechanism: Array.prototype.sort with an inconsistent Math.random comparator (sort order 'implementation-defined' per ECMA-262), run against Fisher–Yates thousands of times per frame and tallied into live 12×12 deviation canvases; no storage, no network.
references: Hans (Jean) Arp, Untitled (Collage with Squares Arranged According to the Laws of Chance), 1916-17
y-a-v-a, Arranged According to the Laws of Chance (2026)
Microsoft EU Browser Choice ballot screen (2010) and Rob Weir's analysis of its biased shuffle
ECMA-262, Array.prototype.sort: implementation-defined order for inconsistent comparators
